AC2.evidence: Fix-pass at scripts/lib/react_template.tpl:1525-1532 tags mealEntry._slotId = mealType in TimelineView.add() so each meal Timeline entry carries its source slot regardless of displayed name. Slot resolver at L1738-1769 now prefers entry._slotId over name-match (with name-fallback for backward compat). AC11.evidence: Fix-pass at scripts/lib/react_template.tpl:2243-2258 introduces _flashReject(el) helper (idempotent, throttled with 500ms el.__rejectAt guard, clears via 400ms setTimeout). Helper is invoked in ALL 6 incompatible onDragOver branches BEFORE the existing dropEffect='none'; return — covering Kanban meal slot-drop (L911), Cafe slot-drop (L996), Activity slot-drop (L1082), Entertainment slot-drop (L1168), Accommodation slot-drop (L1311), and Timeline slot-drop (L1919). Also wired into onDrop and onClick reject branches. 18 _flashReject( call sites in served HTML (6 slots × 3 handlers). The dropEffect='none' is preserved so the native browser cursor still signals 'no drop'; in addition, data-drop-reject is now set on the .slot-drop during the dragOver phase (NOT in the suppressed drop handler), and the existing CSS animation-name=slot-drop-reject-flash + red outline/bg renders the visible feedback. This is a real user-visible feedback gap: a user attempting an incompatible drag sees only the browser's no-drop cursor with no in-app indication that their drag was rejected.

AC13.cross_meal_caveat: AC13 only tested SAME-meal drag (dinner-2-2 → dinner timeline slot). The cross-meal scenario (breakfast-2-1 → dinner timeline slot) is covered under AC2's Timeline-half, which FAILS due to the name-based timeline slot resolution issue. AC13 itself doesn't strictly require cross-meal Timeline support beyond what AC2 requires; this is captured as the AC2 Timeline-half failure above.

all_findings.issue: Timeline entries resolve their slot id by name-matching the displayed entry name against editorDay.slots[*].options[*].name_local. After a cross-meal injection (e.g., breakfast-2-1 occupies dinner.meals slot), the dinner-time Timeline entry's displayed name is '晨曦豆花米线' which matches breakfast.options[*] FIRST. Result: the Timeline dinner entry vanishes — there is no [data-timeline-entry][data-slot-id='dinner'] in the DOM after the cross-meal drop.
all_findings.user_visible_impact: When user drags a breakfast candidate onto the dinner slot in Kanban view, switching to Timeline view they see only one breakfast entry (at 09:00), no entry at 19:00 (dinner-time slot). The dinner timeline row disappears entirely. This contradicts AC2's expectation that the swap should be visible on both Kanban AND Timeline.
all_findings.recommendation: Per Codex finding 5: In TimelineView's add(primary, 'meal', ...) call at react_template.tpl:1525, set entry._slotId = mealType explicitly when pushing. Then in the resolution loop at L1717-1737, prefer entry._slotId over name-based lookup. This decouples timeline slot identity from displayed-name matching.

all_findings.issue: When dragging an incompatible candidate over a slot, onDragOver sets dataTransfer.dropEffect='none' and returns early. The browser's HTML5 drag system then suppresses the drop event entirely. The onDrop handler — which contains the data-drop-reject + 400ms setTimeout logic — never fires. Result: no visible in-app feedback during incompatible drag; only the browser's native no-drop cursor signals rejection.
all_findings.user_visible_impact: A user dragging a meal candidate onto a non-meal slot sees only the cursor change to a 🚫 icon. No red flash on the target. The AC11 spec explicitly requires data-drop-reject + visible CSS feedback on drag-reject.
all_findings.recommendation: Per Codex finding 1: Add a shared _flashReject(el) helper that sets data-drop-reject and removes it after 400-600ms. Call it inside every incompatible onDragOver branch BEFORE returning early. Keep dropEffect='none' for the native cursor signal. Mirror the same pattern as _flashSuccess.
all_findings.note: The click-based reject path (tap-to-select onto incompatible slot) works correctly and provides visible feedback — but this is a separate UX path and does not satisfy AC11's drag-reject requirement.

all_findings.location: BA spec AC1 (and similar Chinese-name negative substring predicates)
all_findings.issue: AC1's predicate 'AFTER textContent MUST NOT INCLUDE 云线楼' is too literal — it does not account for adjacent option names appearing in notes_local descriptions. After dinner-2-2 (建新园) replaces dinner-2-1, the new card's notes contain '比云线楼更实惠更传统' (comparison clause), which trips the negative substring check even though the semantic swap is correct.
all_findings.recommendation: Per Codex finding 2: tighten AC1's predicate to assert against the meal name line specifically (e.g., the first text segment after the emoji), not whole-card textContent.
